newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ATHLETICS-BOLDON, BAILEY, GREENE SET FOR SHOWDOWN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BOLDON, BAILEY, GREENE SET FOR SHOWDOWN.

text.p: Ato Boldon, Maurice Greene and Donovan Bailey look set for a fascinating 100 metres sprint showdown at next month's Athens world championships after flourishing in Scandanavian sunshine over the past four days.
Trinidad's Boldon, the Olympic 100 and 200 bronze medallist, completed a 100-200 double in Monday's Stockholm Grand Prix, the penultimate meeting before the world championships open on August 1.
He also set a year's fastest time of 19.82 seconds in the 200, beating American 100 champion Greene into second place.
Boldon, beaten by Greene over 100 metres in heavy rain in Lausanne last week, relished the still, hot Stockholm evening.
"I have got to learn to run better in the rain," he said. "I have never run well in the rain and it has been raining."
Boldon has been training in California with Greene under the guidance of John Smith, probably the world's most successful sprint coach.
"Training with Maurice...if you look up you're a distant third," Boldon said.

"The big change I have had is going out to California and training with new coach John Smith and Ato Boldon," he said. "I'm learning new things every day. I still have a lot more to learn about the race."
Bailey won the 200 metres at Friday's Bislett Games in Oslo but does not intend to double up in Athens.
"I have no intention of running both," he said after the meeting. "But I'd like to break the national record and maybe go under 20 seconds for the 200.
"I'm going back to Austin, Texas, to train for the national championships on July 18."
